title: I built a loop where an AI plays, critiques and rewrites its own game, streamed live daily. Day 1 is tonight.
author: Playful-Leek9091
selftext:
Every day at 7 PM ET, Claude Opus 5.5 plays its own browser game, critiques it, rewrites the code and plays again, live on YouTube. Nobody touches the code.


To play, it looks at screenshots, and the game pauses while it decides each move, so the delay between decisions doesn't matter. Each new version has to pass a check before it goes live; if it fails, the old version stays.


It starts from one jumping square and has to keep it, so it can't start over. It also keeps a design notebook between episodes, so the game builds up over time. It runs from a Raspberry Pi 5, with about $7 to spend each episode.


Will it be a real game by Day 30, or 30 days of fiddling with jump physics?


Day 1: [https://youtu.be/spFR0-LvCGc](https://youtu.be/spFR0-LvCGc)

comments.author: pol-delta
comments.body: So how long does it actually stream for if the budget is $7 per day?

replies.author: Playful-Leek9091
replies.body: Day 1 ran about 53 minutes before hitting the $7 cap. My rules were too loose, so the AI rewrote the whole game every round. Now it only edits what changes, so Day 2 should run the full hour.
